That sentence is programmatically determined link context and gives the purpose: the FGV Portal do Titular, where you manage your personal data and unsubscribe. The address's path says the same. judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The image is the thumbnail of the YouTube video 'Campanha Vestibular FGV', alt="", the only content of div.video-embed-field-launch-modal. That div opens the video in a modal on click and has no role, name or tabindex, in the snapshot and in the live HTML. The thumbnail file does contain the burned-in subtitle 'que abrem portas.', and the text around it does not, so the sentence is true of the capture. In my view the element fails 1.1.1: as the sole content of the video launcher, it is the only sign that a video is there, and screen readers get nothing. But the claim rests on an incidental subtitle fragment, not on what the image needs to convey. Competent auditors would disagree on whether that names the real defect, and on whether the failure belongs to 1.1.1 or to 2.1.1/4.1.2 for the div.
